KL-000.nextGate: the independent implementation re-runs against protocol v1.1.0. This is a separate commission by the owner; this repository's agents do not execute it and do not modify impl-rs. What it tests: whether the R1 conclusion function, the R4 canonical form (via C11's pinned contentDigest -- the first KL-000 value a second implementation can be wrong about rather than merely different from), and the R2/R3 admissibility rules close the 22,440-world divergence. Exact pass condition: identical conclusion distribution on all 110,840 receipt-producing exhaustive worlds AND a matching C11 digest. For a stronger independence claim the re-run should occur on a machine that does not hold the reference at all (operator's own remediation, OPERATOR-DISCLOSURE.md).
KL-000.claimAllowed: Within the declared bounds, the reference evaluator did not allow a recorded copy to change evidential mass, and did not allow an incomplete search to yield an absence conclusion; it conforms to protocol v1.1.0; and the four v1.1.0 repairs documented behaviour it already had (no number moved). An independent implementation written from the registered documents alone reproduced the exhaustive enumeration exactly and passed all ten v1.0.0 invariants over it.

F1/F2: I2 and I5 are stated receipt-internally and are vacuously satisfiable (open; v1.2.0 candidate)
F3: B2 and B3 may be one ablation counted twice (open)
F4/F5: conversionsToReverse undefined at the empty ledger; margin sign unpinned, 38,760 worlds' receipts differ between readings (open)
F11: the frozen seed freezes no cross-implementation stream; randomized comparisons are replications only (open)
F12: the adversarial phase is defined by reference to a test file, not by specification (open)
F13: C06's fixture note contradicts C04 and C07 (open)
F14: unavailable is reported and reconciled but no conclusion depends on it (open)
KL-000.quantitativeCaveat: 75.7% of randomized worlds fail closed and produce no receipt, so most invariants were exercised on 243,381 randomized worlds rather than 1,000,000; the 95% rule-of-three upper bound for those is 1.23e-5 per receipt-producing world. The independent implementation's randomized counts are not comparable quantities to the reference's (different world streams; finding F11).
KL-000.stateNote: adversarial-passed under BOTH protocol v1.0.0 (RUN-20260807-1) and protocol v1.1.0 (RUN-20260807-2). NOT verified-independent: the independent reimplementation agreed on all ten v1.0.0 invariants over an exactly-reproduced exhaustive enumeration but disagreed on the conclusion of 22,440 of 110,840 receipt-producing worlds, over a conclusion function v1.0.0 left open. v1.1.0 repair R1 has since decided that function; the independent implementation has not yet run against v1.1.0.
